params.body:
## What

- **/communities** names its first community, KUBO CyberSec in The Gambia, links to its page, and keeps a card open for the clubs to come. The "Soon" label is gone. Same in nl and fr; the nl and fr copies had one sentence spliced into the middle of another, which the new card replaces.
- **/communities/cybersec** (with /nl and /fr copies): what the community is, who it is for, how to join, and its first event, a Capture the Flag on Saturday 14 November 2026 at the IT Lab, Bakoteh Proper LBS, 10:00 to 17:00. Every fact comes from the poster: free entry, teams, all levels with beginners welcome, lunch, prizes and certificates, organised by Afrodidact The Gambia and the KUBO CyberSec Community. The page also shows the poster (webp at 848 and 480 px, explicit dimensions, descriptive alt text, JPG download), the community's sudo ./learn keycap sticker in the header (webp with alpha), and schema.org Event data.
- The content lives in one component (`src/components/CyberSecPage.astro`), so the event facts cannot drift between the three languages. The translations are kept plain; the nl and fr alt text says the poster itself is in English.

## After 14 November

The page switches by date. The build decides whether the event is upcoming or past, and a small inline script checks again in the browser. After 17:00 on 14 November the registration box gives way to a "took place" note, even if the site has not been rebuilt (Netlify only builds on push). A build after the date leaves the registration box, and the encoded number, out of the HTML entirely. I checked this with a build under a clock set to 15 November.

## Contact number kept out of reach of scrapers

- The number is not in the source or the built site as digits. The page holds an encoded form (`src/lib/contact.js`), and a "Show number" button decodes it in the browser on click and shows it as written on the poster. There is no `tel:` or `wa.me` link. Without JS the box points to info@kubo.global.
- On the served poster copies (both webp sizes and the JPG), the number after "REGISTER: MESSAGE ALPHA" is painted out in the poster's own dark background. Nothing else on the poster changed, and the original poster is not in the repo. The alt text refers to the page for the number.
- `npm run check:built` walks every text file in `dist/` and fails if any form of the number appears. It is now a CI step after the build. Unit tests in `tests/contact.test.js` cover the encoding and the matching, and the tests contain only the encoded form. In SVG files the check only counts the longer forms, because an existing logo has a path coordinate that matches the last four digits.

## Checks

- `npm run test:coverage`: 25 tests pass.
- `npm run build`: clean. `npm run check:built`: no contact number in 80 text files.
- Looked at by screenshot on desktop and phone, in all three languages, with the register box before and after the click and without JS. No horizontal overflow on phone.
params.title: Communities: name KUBO CyberSec, give it a page with its first event
